issue.body:
### Description

Hi JAX,

I'm using JAX in Colab for development, which involves running some reasonably GPU memory intensive functions.  This memory should be, and is, de-allocated after execution.  

However, if the call errors in an unhandled way during execution, the GPU memory is not released, effectively filling up the GPU while I'm debugging erroneous code.  

I made a Colab for repro [here](https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1QUA1m_H494fewnOEsx-w4WycfwI37EbC?usp=sharing).

I'm not sure if this is a JAX/XLA bug/idiosyncrasy, if it is something to do with Colab, or if this is something that is a one-off.  

Do you have advice for de-allocating the memory allocated during the call prior to crashing?  (its deeply irritating having to restart the runtime and re-run all the preceding code every time haha!)

You can also see in the Nvidia-smi output posted above, that there are no processes on the GPU, but that 777mb is allocated (/lost)?

Thanks,
Andy

### What jax/jaxlib version are you using?

jax==0.4.4

### Which accelerator(s) are you using?

GPU

### Additional system info

_No response_
